subject: Mutual success plan & acceptance test matrix for Novatech evaluation
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@novatech.com>, Ben O'Neil <ben.oneil@novatech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual success plan & acceptance test matrix for Novatech evaluation

Hi Alicia / Ben,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our call, I sketched a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a candidate acceptance-test matrix to make the evaluation deterministic and shorten your path to a decision. Attaching a draft spreadsheet (MAP_Novatech_v3.xlsx) with timeline rows and a separate CSV with concrete test rows.

High-level goals we proposed on the call (please confirm or correct):
- Goal A: Integrate Redwood API with Novatech ingestion pipeline and validate inference quality on your 20k sample prompts by July 14.
- Goal B: Meet production latency envelope: P95 generation < 250ms for 512 token context on our Dedicated profile or fallback hosted variant.
- Goal C: Confirm security artifacts (SOC2, encryption at rest, audit logs) for procurement.

Suggested exit gates (minimum viable criteria to pass evaluation):
1) Functional: 95% of core intent prompts return acceptable labels per your rubric (see sheet 'Quality Rubric').
2) Performance: P95 latency < 250ms and sustained throughput of 40 reqs/sec on Dedicated config during 30-minute soak.
3) Cost guardrail: estimated per-token cost <= $0.0007 in projected production workload.
4) Security: SOC2 report and KMS integration validated, plus successful audit log export.

Acceptance tests (examples in the spreadsheet):
- Integration smoke: end-to-end request from ingestion -> Redwood -> application UI with synthetic workload (owner: Novatech dev team, date: Jul 7).
- Quality spot-check: 1k annotated prompts reviewed against rubric (owner: Novatech/Redwood joint, date: Jul 10).
- Latency soak: 30-min load run at target throughput (owner: Redwood SRE, date: Jul 12).

Next steps I propose:
1) You review the attached MAP and mark any missing items by EOD Thu Jul 2.
2) We'll lock owners and exact test data sets by Mon Jul 6.
3) Run acceptance tests Jul 10–14 and sync on results Jul 15.

I left some cells blank for owners and data links — please fill in where you can. If the timeline is too aggressive, say so and we'll adjust.

Attachments: MAP_Novatech_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), novatech-acceptance-test-matrix.csv (CSV)

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Thanks Neha — this looks close to what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications from my side: 

1) Quality rubric: we'll share our label set (approx 1k labels) by Fri Jul 3. Can Redwood run the automated scoring against that set or do you need us to upload to a specific S3 bucket?
2) Latency: our on-prem app is sensitive to cold-starts. Can the soak include a second run that ramps from idle to load so we can capture cold-start behavior?
3) Security: we'll need the list of actionable evidence for procurement. Can you confirm which items you can provide within one business day (SOC2, encryption details, audit log format)?

Also, please add a row to the MAP for a live walkthrough of the evaluation results (ideally Jul 15 or Jul 16). Ben will join that call.

Alicia
Director of Platform, Novatech Inc.
alicia@novatech.com

- Quality scoring: Redwood can run automated scoring if Novatech provides the labeled set as CSV or a shared Drive link. Please provide by end of day Fri Jul 3. (Owner: Alicia / Novatech)
- Cold-starts: yes — we will include a two-phase soak: 1) cold-start ramp 2) steady-state. We'll capture both P95 and cold-start 95th/99th percentiles. (Owner: Redwood SRE - Rishi)
- Security artifacts: we can provide SOC2 Type II summary, KMS integration notes, and sample audit log export. Full evidence package may require an NDA addendum for some items; I'll coordinate with legal if needed.

Internal asks (Marissa / Karthik / Rishi):
- Marissa: please prep the runbook for the latency soak and include the exact test harness (JMeter/Locust) configuration. Target date to share runbook: Jul 9.
- Karthik: can you validate the cost model row in the MAP. We estimated per-token cost at $0.00065 for the Dedicated profile given the projected QPS; please confirm.
- Rishi: can you confirm SRE availability Jul 11–13 for the soak windows and that we can capture per-route traces for the report?

I'll update the Google Drive MAP folder with a new tab called 'Owners & Dates' after internal confirmation.

Neha

Quick SRE/technical confirmation and proposed concrete acceptance checks to put in the test matrix. Please review and call out anything we missed.

Top-level SRE commitments:
- SRE will run soak windows Jul 11 (dry run) and Jul 12 (official). Engineer on-call: Rishi Malhotra.
- We'll provide per-request traces, KV cache hit rates, and a latency heatmap for the test period.

Technical acceptance checks (pass/fail):
1) Latency envelope: P95 generation < 250ms AND cold-start 95th < 1.2s during ramp. Pass if both hold for official run.
2) Throughput: sustain 40 reqs/sec for 30 minutes with error rate < 0.5%.
3) Deterministic outputs: for 1k canonical prompts, exact top-1 label stability across 3 runs (we'll allow non-determinism window for sampling models; see doc).
4) Resource limits: GPU memory usage < 85% avg and no OOM events during soak.
5) Security smoke: audit log delivered in JSONL format to a Novatech S3 bucket and verified schema.

I'll add these rows to novatech-acceptance-test-matrix.csv and upload to the shared Drive. Marissa — I'll need the load scripts and exact seed values by Jul 9. Karthik — please confirm the cost sensitivity analysis cell I updated.

Rishi
Lead SRE, Redwood Inference
